words: وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى
rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliyah describes the daylight of Paradise as lasting about the time people pray the dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العالية: نهار الجنة هكذا: وأشار إلى ساعة المصلين صلاة الفجر.

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd says the road becomes visible and apparent when it is exposed to the sun.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زيد: ضحا الطريق يضحو ضحوا إذا بدا لك وظهر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ضحيت can mean sweating, or coming out into the sun; both forms ضحيت and ضحيت are reported, with أضحى as the future in either usage.
rows.anchor: وضحيت وضحيت بالكسر ضحا عرقت. وضحيت أيضا للشمس ضحاء ممدود برزت

rows.speaker: عمر بن أبي ربيعة
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abi Rabiʿa's line uses يضحى for being exposed to the sun, supporting the lexical explanation.
rows.anchor: قال عمر بن أبي ربيعة: رأت رجلا أيما إذا الشمس عارضت فيضحى

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar told a pilgrim who had shaded himself, “Expose yourself for the One for whom you entered ihram”; hadith transmitters vocalize أضح as أضحيت.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث أن ابن عمر رأى رجلا محرما قد استظل، فقال: أضح لمن أحرمت له.

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿi corrects the wording to اِضْحَ from ضحيت أضحى, meaning to expose oneself to the sun; he cites the verse and a poem.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: إنما هو اضح لمن أحرمت له بكسر الألف وفتح الحاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed poetic line uses ضحيت for coming out into sunlight, as shown by the contrast with a shrinking shadow.
rows.anchor: ضحيت له كي أستظل بظله إذا الظل أضحى في القيامة قالصا

words: وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى
rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والكوفيون إلا عاصما في رواية أبي بكر
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr and the Kufans except ʿAsim in Abu Bakr's transmission read وأنك with an open hamza, coordinating it with ألا تجوع.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو والكوفيون إلا عاصما في رواية أبي بكر عنه «وأنك» بفتح الهمزة

words: وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the open hamza, وأنك may also be nominative by coordination with the syntactic position, meaning that you will not thirst there.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع عطفا على الموضع، والمعنى: ولك أنك لا تظمأ فيها

words: وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى
rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use a kasra on إنك, treating it as a new sentence or coordinating it with إن لك.
rows.anchor: الباقون بالكسر على الاستئناف، أو على العطف على «إن لك».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual command addresses Adam and Iblis, and منها means the Garden; the command to expel Iblis in 7:18 may imply an initial expulsion to a heavenly place before descent to earth.
rows.anchor: خاطب آدم وإبليس. «منها» أي من الجنة. وقد قال لإبليس: اخرج منها مذءوما مدحورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam is hostile to the serpent and Iblis, while both are hostile to him; this rules out Adam and Eve as the two addressed, since they were not enemies, though Eve's descent is included in Adam's.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن قوله: «اهبطا» ليس خطابا لآدم وحواء لأنهما ما كانا متعاديين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance here means right direction and true speech; Qurtubi says its explanation was given earlier in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: أي رشدا وقولا حقا. وقد تقدم في «البقرة».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance to be followed refers to the messengers and scriptures.
rows.anchor: يعني الرسل والكتب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God guarantees that whoever recites the Qur'an and acts on it will not stray in this world or suffer in the Hereafter, and he recited this verse.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ضمن الله تعالى لمن قرأ القرآن وعمل بما فيه ألا يضل في الدنيا، ولا يشقى في الآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In another report, Ibn ʿAbbas says whoever reads and follows the Qur'an is guided from error and protected from a bad reckoning on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: وعنه: من قرأ القرآن واتبع ما فيه هداه الله من الضلالة، ووقاه يوم القيامة سوء الحساب، ثم تلا الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr may mean God's religion, reciting His Book, and acting by it; it may instead mean the revealed proofs, or the Messenger as the source of the reminder.
rows.anchor: أي ديني، وتلاوة كتابي، والعمل بما فيه. وقيل: عما أنزلت من الدلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضنك describes a constricted dwelling or life and has the same form for singular, dual, masculine, feminine, and plural.
rows.anchor: أي عيشا ضيقا يقال: منزل ضنك وعيش ضنك يستوي فيه الواحد والاثنان والمذكر والمؤنث

rows.speaker: عنترة
rows.claim: Antarah uses بضنك for a constricted or difficult place in two lines, illustrating the word's usage.
rows.anchor: قال عنترة: إن يلحقوا أكرر وإن يستلحموا أشدد وإن يلفوا بضنك أنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading has ضنكى on the فعلى pattern.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «ضنكى» على وزن فعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion brings submission, contentment, and trust in God and His allotment, so the believer spends easily and lives abundantly; Qurtubi links this to the good life promised in 16:97.
rows.anchor: أن الله عز وجل جعل مع الدين التسليم والقناعة والتوكل عليه وعلى قسمته، فصاحبه ينفق مما رزقه الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning from religion lets acquisitive greed and miserliness dominate, making life constricted and dark; one reported saying adds that the person's time darkens and livelihood becomes troubled.
rows.anchor: والمعرض عن الدين مستول عليه الحرص الذي لا يزال يطمح به إلى الازدياد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima interprets the constricted life as unlawful earnings.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: «ضنكا» كسبا حراما

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets it as the food of ḍarīʿ and zaqqum.
rows.anchor: الحسن: طعام الضريع والزقوم

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وعبد الله بن مسعود وأبو هريرة
rows.claim: Qurtubi calls the fourth interpretation correct: punishment in the grave, stated by Abu Saʿid and Ibn Masʿud and reported marfuʿ by Abu Hurayra from the Prophet; the unbeliever's grave tightens until his ribs interlock. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وقول رابع وهو الصحيح أنه عذاب القبر قاله أبو سعيد الخدري وعبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation that a person is blind in one state and sighted in another was discussed at the end of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ.
rows.anchor: قيل: أعمى في حال وبصيرا في حال وقد تقدم في آخر «سبحان».

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the person is blind to the proof.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أعمى عن الحجة قاله مجاهد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say the person is blind to every path of good, or unable to find a way to fend off punishment, like a blind person helpless before what he cannot see.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أعمى عن جهات الخير، لا يهتدي لشيء منها. وقيل: عن الحيلة في دفع العذاب عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker asks what sin brought punishment by blindness; his question suggests that he thinks himself guiltless.
rows.anchor: أي بأي ذنب عاقبتني بالعمى. { وقد كنت بصيرا } أي في الدنيا، وكأنه يظن أنه لا ذنب له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He had been sighted in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي في الدنيا، وكأنه يظن أنه لا ذنب له.

words: لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid understand blindness as blindness to his proof, and sightedness as knowing his proof in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد: أي { قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى } عن حجتي { وقد كنت بصيرا } أي عالما بحجتي

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri's gloss that the unbeliever knew his proof is far-fetched, Qurtubi says, since an unbeliever had no proof in this world.
rows.anchor: القشيري: وهو بعيد إذ ما كان للكافر حجة في الدنيا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's signs are proofs of His oneness and power.
rows.anchor: أي دلالاتنا على وحدانيتنا وقدرتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting here means abandoning the signs, failing to consider them, and turning away from them.
rows.anchor: أي تركتها ولم تنظر فيها، وأعرضت عنها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being forgotten today means being left in punishment, namely Hell.
rows.anchor: أي تترك في العذاب يريد جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God likewise repays those who turn from the Qur'an and reflection on created things, and transgress the bounds through sin.
rows.anchor: وكما جزينا من أعرض عن القرآن، وعن النظر في المصنوعات، والتفكر فيها، وجاوز الحد في المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not believing in the Lord's signs means not affirming them as true.
rows.anchor: أي لم يصدق بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment of the Hereafter is more terrible than the constricted life and punishment of the grave.
rows.anchor: أي أفظع من المعيشة الضنك، وعذاب القبر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hereafter's punishment is more enduring and stable because it never ends or ceases.
rows.anchor: أي أدوم وأثبت لأنه لا ينقطع ولا ينقضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan unbelievers demanded a sign from Muhammad that compelled certain knowledge, a manifest sign like the she-camel or staff, or the specific signs they requested as earlier peoples had.
rows.anchor: يريد كفار مكة أي لولا يأتينا محمد بآية توجب العلم الضروري. أو بآية ظاهرة كالناقة والعصا.

words: أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier scriptures—the Torah, Gospel, and prior books—are themselves a greater sign because Muhammad reported their contents.
rows.anchor: يريد التوراة والإنجيل والكتب المتقدمة، وذلك أعظم آية إذ أخبر بما فيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant lightens the pronunciation of الصحف.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «الصحف» بالتخفيف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the proof as the prophecies of Muhammad found in earlier scriptures, which attest his prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أولم تأتهم الآية الدالة على نبوته بما وجدوه في الكتب المتقدمة من البشارة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the proof is God's destruction of earlier peoples who rejected and demanded signs; the Meccans might suffer the same fate if signs came.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أولم يأتهم إهلاكنا الأمم الذين كفروا واقترحوا الآيات فما يؤمنهم إن أتتهم الآيات

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وابن أبي إسحاق وحفص
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Yaʿqub, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Hafs read تأتهم with feminine ت to agree with البينة.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وابن أبي إسحاق وحفص «أولم تأتهم» بالتاء لتأنيث البينة.

rows.speaker: الباقون وأبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: The remaining readers use ي, reflecting the earlier verb position or treating البينة as البيان والبرهان; Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim prefer this reading.
rows.anchor: الباقون بالياء لتقدم الفعل ولأن البينة هي البيان والبرهان فردوه إلى المعنى

rows.speaker: الكسائي والنحاس
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi transmits the construction; al-Nahhas says if بينة is indefinite and nominative, ما is its apposition, while if accusative it is circumstantial, meaning the earlier-scripture content came manifestly.
rows.anchor: وحكى الكسائي «أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى» قال: ويجوز على هذا «بينة ما في الصحف الأولى». قال النحاس: إذا نونت «بينة» ورفعت جعلت «ما» بدلا

words: ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypothetical destruction is before Muhammad's mission and the Qur'an's descent; the doomed would have asked on Judgment Day why no messenger had been sent to them.
rows.anchor: أي من قبل بعثة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ونزول القرآن { لقالوا } أي يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid reports a Prophetic account: people who died in the interval, the mentally incapacitated, and infants voice excuses; a fire is raised as a test, and their response distinguishes the one who would have obeyed from the one who would not.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الهالك في الفترة والمعتوه والمولود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb فنتبع is subjunctive as the response to the preceding solicitation.
rows.anchor: { فنتبع } نصب بجواب التخصيص.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آياتك refers to what Muhammad brought.
rows.anchor: { آياتك } يريد ما جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says they fear humiliation in punishment and disgrace in Hell.
rows.anchor: { ونخزى } في جهنم قاله ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view assigns humiliation to punishment in this world and disgrace to punishment in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا بالعذاب { ونخزى } في الآخرة بعذابها.

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The report about afterlife testing is also transmitted as a statement of Abu Saʿid rather than raised to the Prophet; Qurtubi questions it, discusses it in al-Tadhkira, and notes its use by advocates of testing children and others in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: ويروى موقوفا عن أبي سعيد قوله وفيه نظر وقد بيناه في كتاب «التذكرة» وبه احتج من قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to say that believers and unbelievers alike await what time will bring and which side will win.
rows.anchor: أي قل لهم يا محمد كل متربص، أي كل المؤمنين والكافرين منتظر دوائر الزمان ولمن يكون النصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The level path is the upright religion and guidance; victory will show who follows the true religion.
rows.anchor: يريد الدين المستقيم والهدى والمعنى: فستعلمون بالنصر من اهتدى إلى دين الحق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view places the recognition on Judgment Day, when people will know who was guided to the path of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فستعلمون يوم القيامة من اهتدى إلى طريق الجنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse closes the sūra with a threat, warning, and intimidation.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا ضرب من الوعيد والتخويف والتهديد ختم به السورة.

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: A reading has فسوف تعلمون; Abu Rafiʿ says he memorized it from the Prophet, as cited by al-Zamakhshari.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «فسوف تعلمون». قال أبو رافع: حفظته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكره الزمخشري.

rows.speaker: الزجاج والفراء وأبو إسحاق والنحاس
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses من as nominative; al-Farraʾ allows accusative like 2:220. Abu Ishaq objects that an interrogative cannot be governed by what precedes and parses it as an initial subject: are we or you on the straight path?
rows.anchor: و«من» في موضع رفع عند الزجاج. وقال الفراء: يجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب مثل والله يعلم المفسد من المصلح

words: من أصحاب الصراط السوي ومن اهتدى
rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas explains al-Farraʾ's sense as asking who did not stray and who strayed before becoming guided.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: والفراء يذهب إلى أن معنى { من أصحاب الصراط السوي } من لم يضل

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر وعاصم الجحدري
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Yaʿmar and ʿAsim al-Jahdari read السوا with a doubled wāw and feminine alif, on fuʿla; making الصراط feminine is rare, whereas 1:6 uses the masculine.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر وعاصم الجحدري «فسيعلمون من أصحاب الصراط السوا» بتشديد الواو بعدها ألف التأنيث

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim rejects السوا: from سوء it should be السوءى, and from سواء it should be السيا with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقد رد هذا أبو حاتم قال: إن كان من السوء وجب أن يقال السوءى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the reading السواء can mean the middle, justice, or what is straight.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وقرىء «السواء» بمعنى الوسط والعدل أو المستوي.

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas allows the reading by positing original السوءى, with the hamza replaced by wāw after a preceding ḍamma.
rows.anchor: النحاس: وجواز قراءة يحيى بن يعمر والجحدري أن يكون الأصل «السوءى»

words: وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي
rows.speaker: عكرمة وعطية وابن زيد وابن عباس
rows.claim: A third interpretation, reported from ʿIkrima, ʿAtiyya, Ibn Zayd, and Ibn ʿAbbas, says the heavens could not rain and the earth could not grow; God opened the sky with rain and earth with plants.
rows.anchor: وقول ثالث قاله عكرمة وعطية وابن زيد وابن عباس أيضا فيما ذكر المهدوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says this interpretation is witnessed directly, and that God mentions it in several verses to demonstrate His power and the resurrection and requital.
rows.anchor: وبه يقع الاعتبار مشاهدة ومعاينة ولذلك أخبر بذلك في غير ما آية ليدل على كمال قدرته

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari chooses the interpretation of sky and earth being closed and then opened because the next phrase says every living thing was made from water.
rows.anchor: واختار هذا القول الطبري لأن بعده { وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي أفلا يؤمنون }

words: وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God created everything from water.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى: { وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي } ثلاث تأويلات: أحدها: أنه خلق كل شيء من الماء قاله قتادة.

words: وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is that water preserves the life of everything.
rows.anchor: الثاني حفظ حياة كل شيء بالماء

words: وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي
rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub says every living thing was made from seminal fluid.
rows.anchor: الثالث: وجعلنا من ماء الصلب كل شيء حي قاله قطرب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here جعلنا means خلقنا, “We created.”
rows.anchor: «وجعلنا» بمعنى خلقنا.

words: وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hatim al-Busti reports from Abu Hurayra that he asked the Prophet about everything, and the Prophet replied that everything was created from water; Abu Hatim treats this as a sound report and says the question meant all created things.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو حاتم البستي في المسند الصحيح له من حديث أبي هريرة قال: قلت: يا رسول الله! إذا رأيتك

words: وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophetic reply that everything was created from water is an additional proof, alongside the opening of heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: وهذا احتجاج آخر سوى ما تقدم من كون السموات والأرض رتقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi notes that الكل may sometimes mean only part, and begins to cite a supporting example.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الكل قد يذكر بمعنى البعض كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The segment says the seventh earth is called ʿAriba and contains Hell, with two gates named Sijjin and al-Falaq; Sijjin is open and records of unbelievers end there, while al-Falaq stays closed until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ثم خلق الله الأرض السابعة واسمها عريبة وفيها جهنم، فيها بابان اسم الواحد سجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prior discussion in al-Baqara says seven earths lie one above another, with a journey of five hundred years between each pair; further detail is promised at the end of al-Talaq.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى في «البقرة» أنها سبع أرضين بين كل أرضين مسيرة خمسمائة عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain paths are explained as passes, since a mountain gap may or may not be an open, traversable route.
rows.anchor: «سبلا» تفسير الفجاج لأن الفج قد يكون طريقا نافذا مسلوكا وقد لا يكون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the paths let people reach faith by reflecting on them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ليهتدوا بالاعتبار بها إلى دينهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the sky is protected from falling on earth, supported by 22:65.
rows.anchor: أي محفوظا من أن يقع ويسقط على الأرض دليله قوله تعالى: ويمسك السماء أن تقع على الأرض إلا بإذنه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the sky is guarded by stars against devils, as in 15:17.
rows.anchor: وقيل: محفوظا بالنجوم من الشياطين قاله الفراء. دليله قوله تعالى: وحفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say the sky is protected from demolition and breach, from being reached by human devices, or needs no supporting pillars.
rows.anchor: وقيل: محفوظا من الهدم والنقض، وعن أن يبلغه أحد بحيلة. وقيل: محفوظا فلا يحتاج إلى عماد.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses محفوظا as raised.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: مرفوعا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the sky is protected from associating partners with God and from sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل: محفوظا من الشرك والمعاصي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They refers to the unbelievers; Mujahid says the signs at issue are the sun and moon.
rows.anchor: يعني الكفار { عن آياتها معرضون } قال مجاهد! يعني الشمس والقمر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are attributed to heaven because they are placed there, though elsewhere they are attributed to God as their maker; the unbelievers fail to reflect on its signs and the divine power they show.
rows.anchor: وأضاف الآيات إلى السماء لأنها مجعولة فيها، وقد أضاف الآيات إلى نفسه في مواضع، لأنه الفاعل لها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had they considered the sky, night and day, sun, moon, orbits, winds, and clouds, they would know one powerful creator and see that He cannot have a partner.
rows.anchor: بين أن المشركين غفلوا عن النظر في السموات وآياتها، من ليلها ونهارها، وشمسها وقمرها، وأفلاكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night was made for rest and day for people to pursue their livelihoods.
rows.anchor: ذكرهم نعمة أخرى: جعل لهم الليل ليسكنوا فيه، والنهار ليتصرفوا فيه لمعايشهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun marks daytime and the moon nighttime, enabling people to know months, years, and reckoning, as explained earlier in al-Israʾ.
rows.anchor: أي وجعل الشمس آية النهار، والقمر آية الليل لتعلم الشهور والسنون والحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “All” includes the sun, moon, stars, planets, night, and day.
rows.anchor: يعني من الشمس والقمر والنجوم والكواكب والليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The celestial bodies run swiftly, like a swimmer moving through water; 79:3 and the name for a horse extending its forelegs in a run illustrate the image.
rows.anchor: أي يجرون ويسيرون بسرعة كالسابح في الماء. قال الله تعالى وهو أصدق القائلين:

rows.speaker: سيبويه والفراء
rows.claim: Sibawayh and al-Farraʾ explain the masculine plural as treating the celestial bodies as rational beings because they obey like rational beings.
rows.anchor: فمذهب سيبويه: أنه لما أخبر عنهن بفعل من يعقل وجعلهن في الطاعة بمنزلة من يعقل

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says the plural form is used to complete the verse ending.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: إنما قال: «يسبحون» لأنه رأس آية

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi illustrates his verse-ending explanation with 54:44, which has منتصر rather than منتصرون.
rows.anchor:
نحن جميع منتصر
[القمر: 44] ولم يقل منتصرون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view assigns the running to the orbits, so the verb is attributed to them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الجري للفلك فنسب إليها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the soundest view is that the planets move in seven spheres below the layered heavens, which are the domain of angels and the causes of the dominion; the moon, Mercury, Venus, sun, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, zodiac, and greatest sphere occupy levels eight and nine as described.
rows.anchor: والأصح أن السيارة تجري في الفلك، وهي سبعة أفلاك دون السموات المطبقة، التي هي مجال الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فلك is the singular of the stellar spheres; the word derives from rotation, as in the round spindle whorl, and describing a woman's breast as tafallaka means it became rounded.
rows.anchor: وأصل الكلمة من الدوران، ومنه فلكة المغزل لاستدارتها. ومنه قيل: فلك ثدي المرأة تفليكا

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr says أفلاك may be pluralized on the fuʿul pattern, like asad/asud and khashab/khashub.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: ويجوز أن يجمع على فعل مثل أسد وأسد وخشب وخشب.

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud's hadith compares a horse he left circling to the sphere, whose stars rotate around it.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث ابن مسعود: تركت فرسي كأنه يدور في فلك. كأنه لدورانه شبهه بفلك السماء

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the spheres are the courses of the stars, sun, and moon between heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: الأفلاك مجاري النجوم والشمس والقمر. قال: وهي بين السماء والأرض.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada describes the sphere as a rotating circle in the sky that carries the stars while the sky itself remains fixed.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الفلك استدارة في السماء تدور بالنجوم مع ثبوت السماء.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid compares the sphere to the iron wheel of a mill and its central pivot.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الفلك كهيئة حديد الرحى وهو قطبها.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the sphere is the celestial body's course and the speed of its movement.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: فلكها مجراها وسرعة مسيرها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view describes the sphere as a contained wave and the course of the sun and moon; God knows best.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الفلك موج مكفوف ومجرى الشمس والقمر فيه والله أعلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turned to one another as people whose argument had failed and who recognized the force of their opponent's case.
rows.anchor: أي رجع بعضهم إلى بعض رجوع المنقطع عن حجته، المتفطن لصحة حجة خصمه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit that they wrong themselves by worshipping idols that cannot speak or protect themselves, let alone help worshippers or avert harm.
rows.anchor: أي بعبادة من لا ينطق بلفظة، ولا يملك لنفسه لحظة، وكيف ينفع عابديه ويدفع عنهم البأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They returned to ignorance and stubbornness and argued that Abraham knew the idols could not speak.
rows.anchor: أي عادوا إلى جهلهم وعنادهم فقالوا: { لقد علمت ما هؤلاء ينطقون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham cuts off their argument by asking why they worship what can neither benefit nor harm them; أف means “filth” or “stinking” for them and their idols.
rows.anchor: أي النتن لكم { ولما تعبدون من دون الله أفلا تعقلون }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Some say they bowed their heads in shame, but Qurtubi objects to that reading of the wording and prefers the sense of reverting to their former position; Ibn ʿAbbas says misery overtook them and they returned to disbelief.
rows.anchor: وفيه نظر لأنه لم يقل نكسوا رءوسهم، بفتح الكاف بل قال: «نكسوا على رءوسهم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Nun is the epithet of Yunus ibn Matta because a fish swallowed him; al-nun means fish.
rows.anchor: أي واذكر «ذا النون» وهو لقب ليونس بن متى لابتلاع النون إياه. والنون الحوت.

rows.speaker: عثمان وثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: A report says ʿUthman told a handsome boy's family to darken his nūna against the evil eye; Thaʿlab transmits from Ibn al-Aʿrabi that nūna is a small child's chin dimple and dssimu means blacken.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث عثمان رضي الله عنه أنه رأى صبيا مليحا فقال: دسموا نونته كي لا تصيبه العين.

rows.speaker: الحسن والشعبي وسعيد بن جبير وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Shaʿbi, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and a report from Ibn Masʿud take مغاضبا as angry with his Lord; al-Tabari and al-Qutaybi chose it, al-Mahdawi approved, and al-Nahhas defends its Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن والشعبي وسعيد بن جبير: مغاضبا لربه عز وجل. واختاره الطبري والقتبي

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas says this is sound Arabic: angry “for” someone means angry on that person's behalf, as in “I became angry for you”; a believer is angered for God when He is disobeyed.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: مغاضبا من أجل ربه، كما تقول: غضبت لك أي من أجلك. والمؤمن يغضب لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most linguists connect the Prophet's words to ʿAʾisha, “Make the stipulation of loyalty for them,” with this usage; al-Qutaybi strongly supports the connection.
rows.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعائشة: «اشترطي لهم الولاء»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report portrays Yunus as narrow-chested under the burdens of prophethood, which crushed him like a weak camel under a heavy load; his anger was a minor lapse, and he was angry for God when punishment was lifted from his people.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر في وصف يونس: إنه كان ضيق الصدر فلما حمل أعباء النبوة تفسخ تحتها

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud says Yunus fled from his Lord's command until ordered to return after the people were spared; they repented when the threatened punishment came, but Yunus left without knowing this and without explicit permission.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: أبق من ربه أي من أمر ربه حتى أمره بالعود إليهم بعد رفع العذاب عنهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God ordered Yunus to go to his people; when Yunus asked to prepare and even requested a sandal, he was told the matter was urgent, and his narrow disposition led him to leave angry.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: أمره الله تعالى بالمسير إلى قومه فسأل أن ينظر ليتأهب، فأعجله الله حتى سأل أن يأخذ نعلا

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Qurtubi calls al-Nahhas's gloss the best: Yunus was angry for his Lord, namely with his people for disbelieving in their Lord.
rows.anchor: فهذا قول وقول النحاس أحسن ما قيل في تأويله.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Dahhak report that Yunus angrily left his people because they were obstinate, though God had commanded him to remain and call them; the passage says he was young and did not bear the full weight of prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه غاضب قومه حين طال عليه أمرهم وتعنتهم فذهب فارا بنفسه، ولم يصبر على أذاهم

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and a group say Yunus left angry with the king who ruled his people.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة منهم الأخفش: إنما خرج مغاضبا للملك الذي كان على قومه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas recounts that the prophet Shaya and King Hizqiya sought a strong, trustworthy Israelite prophet to go to Nineveh's ruler, who had raided Israel and taken captives, and ask him to release them; Yunus questioned whether God had appointed or named him, then left angry with Shaya, the king, and his people.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أراد شعيا النبي والملك الذي كان في وقته اسمه حزقيا أن يبعثوا يونس إلى ملك نينوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that account, Yunus went to the Mediterranean and was swallowed because he abandoned Shaya's command, as 37:142 says; alternatively he was not yet a prophet, but a king's envoy, and after rescue God sent him to the people who then believed.
rows.anchor: فأتى بحر الروم وكان من قصته ما كان فابتلي ببطن الحوت لتركه أمر شعيا

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri considers it likelier that Yunus's anger came after God had sent him and lifted punishment from his people, whom Yunus resented seeing spared.
rows.anchor: وقال القشيري: والأظهر أن هذه المغاضبة كانت بعد إرسال الله تعالى إياه، وبعد رفع العذاب عن القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi calls al-Qushayri's account the best interpretation and says its details will be explained in Sūrat al-Saffat.
rows.anchor: قلت: هذا أحسن ما قيل فيه على ما يأتي بيانه في «والصافات» إن شاء الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Yunus feared his people, who killed anyone caught lying; he fled by ship, admitted being the runaway when the ship stopped, and was swallowed as expiation for a minor lapse.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه كان من أخلاق قومه قتل من جربوا عليه الكذب فخشي أن يقتل فغضب، وخرج فارا على وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion links prophetic lapses to the testing of the believers at Uhud: prophets' sins are forgiven, while such testing can deter repetition; it cites 3:152 and 3:141.
rows.anchor: كما قال في أهل أحد:

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak also says Yunus was angry with his people for rejecting God's messenger, and that everyone should be angry when God is disobeyed.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك أيضا خرج مغاضبا لقومه لأن قومه لما لم يقبلوا منه وهو رسول من الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth view reads غضب as “felt indignation”: Yunus returned after the people were spared, disdained the outcome, and fled. A cited line uses أغضب for “I feel indignation”; Qurtubi objects that indignation still entails anger, so the view cannot say he was angry at no one.
rows.anchor: وقول رابع: إنه لم يغاضب ربه، ولا قومه، ولا الملك، وأنه من قولهم غضب إذا أنف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse أغضب أن تهجى تميم بدارم is cited for using غضب in the sense of feeling affronted or indignant.
rows.anchor: وينشد هذا البيت: وأغضب أن تهجى تميم بدارم أي آنف.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والحسن
rows.claim: One reported gloss says Iblis misled Yunus into thinking God might be unable to punish him; Qurtubi rejects it as unbelief, reporting it from Saʿid ibn Jubayr via al-Mahdawi and from al-Hasan via al-Thaʿlabi.
rows.anchor: قيل: معناه استزله إبليس ووقع في ظنه إمكان ألا يقدر الله عليه بمعاقبته.

rows.speaker: عطاء وسعيد بن جبير والحسن
rows.claim: ʿAta, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, and many scholars interpret the verb as “constrict”; al-Hasan cites 13:26 and 65:7, and Qurtubi says this best fits the reports from Saʿid and al-Hasan.
rows.anchor: وذكر الثعلبي وقال عطاء وسعيد بن جبير وكثير من العلماء معناه: فظن أن لن نضيق عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas also takes قدر as “constrict”; قدر, قتر, and their variants can all carry that sense.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس فيما ذكره الماوردي والمهدوي.

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد والفراء
rows.claim: Qatada, Mujahid, and al-Farraʾ derive the phrase from divine decree and judgment: Yunus thought God would not decree punishment for him, not that God lacked power.
rows.anchor: قاله قتادة ومجاهد والفراء. مأخوذ من القدر وهو الحكم دون القدرة والاستطاعة.

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thaʿlab says the verb is from تقدير rather than قدرة; his cited poem says what God decrees and determines will occur.
rows.anchor: وروى عن أبي العباس أحمد بن يحيى ثعلب، أنه قال في قول الله عز وجل: { فظن أن لن نقدر عليه } هو من التقدير ليس من القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi connects the two interpretations of قدر to the hadith of a man who asked his family to burn and scatter him after death, fearing divine judgment; the hadith appears in the Muwatta and other collections.
rows.anchor: وهذان التأويلان تأولهما العلماء في قول الرجل الذي لم يعمل خيرا قط لأهله إذا مات فحرقوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the constriction reading, the man's words mean that if God constricts him, rigorously reckons with him, and requites his sins, that will be his fate; he then ordered the burning out of extreme fear.
rows.anchor: فعلى التأويل الأول يكون تقديره: والله لئن ضيق الله علي وبالغ في محاسبتي وجزاني على ذنوبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the decree reading, he means that if God had decreed punishment for every sinner, He will punish him as no one else; the hadith is reported by the leading collectors in the Muwatta and elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وعلى التأويل الثاني: أي لئن كان سبق في قدر الله وقضائه أن يعذب كل ذي جرم على جرمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man was a believing monotheist; one version says his only good deed was monotheism, and he said he acted from fear of God, which Qurtubi says only a believing person can feel, citing 35:28.
rows.anchor: والرجل كان مؤمنا موحدا. وقد جاء في بعض طرقه «لم يعمل خيرا إلا التوحيد»

rows.speaker: سليمان أبو المعتمر
rows.claim: Sulayman Abu al-Muʿtamir proposes an interrogative reading with the hamza omitted for brevity: أفظن, “Did he think?”
rows.anchor: الاستفهام وتقديره: أفظن فحذف ألف الاستفهام إيجازا

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري وابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz and al-Zuhri read نُقَدِّر with a ḍamma on ن and doubled د; al-Mawardi also reports this reading from Ibn ʿAbbas.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري: «فظن أن لن نقدر عليه» بضم النون وتشديد الدال من التقدير.

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير وقتادة والأعرج
rows.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, Qatada, and al-Aʿraj read أن لن يقدر عليه with a doubled dāl in the passive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير وقتادة والأعرج: «أن لن يقدر عليه» بضم الياء مشددا على الفعل المجهول.

rows.speaker: يعقوب وعبد الله بن أبي إسحاق والحسن وابن عباس
rows.claim: Yaʿqub, ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Ishaq, al-Hasan, and Ibn ʿAbbas read يقدر عليه with a light dāl in the passive; al-Hasan also has the form فظن أن لن يقدر عليه.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب وعبد الله بن أبي إسحاق والحسن وابن عباس أيضا «يقدر عليه» بياء مضمومة وفتح الدال مخففا على الفعل المجهول.

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use نقدر with an open ن and kasra on د; Qurtubi says all these readings carry the sense of decree.
rows.anchor: الباقون «نقدر» بفتح النون وكسر الدال وكله بمعنى التقدير.
